pairs.subject: production-pipeline-phasing
pairs.evidence: packages/ui/src/components/style/LockGate.tsx:4 A style moves from candidate to proven to locked only through operator keeps and an explicit lock that the server admits only when the trial-coverage gate holds, so the shared style contract graduates by a human act against a checked gate.

techniques.evidence: packages/ui/src/components/style/LockGate.tsx:4 The ratchet is one-way and the lock is an explicit act gated on the server. Graduation is a human act and is not inferred from completion.

packages/ui/src/components/style/ProofSheet.tsx:6 A rejection carries a required note, so it has been decided about and crosses into the asset side. The reference window counts approved proofs only, and stale approvals stop vouching.

packages/ui/src/components/style/style.ts:2 Single writer: status, coverage and blocker are computed once by the server ratchet and never re-derived by a view. proofLook draws a stale approval as idle, not done.
packages/ui/src/components/cut/CutReview.tsx:36 Cut-review notes are addressed by the beat's start second on the export's own clock, so a note has a time address.

pairs.registryProposal: approval-reads-forward assumes a shared asset's downstream beats exist when it is approved. A library-level style contract is locked before any project that will use it has beats, and here its forward read is a fixed battery of generic trial problems. The technique does not name that proxy. Read literally, the rule 'the forward list cannot be written, so the asset is not ready to graduate' would forbid locking any library style. The technique should say whether a stress battery satisfies the forward read for assets shared across projects.

techniques.evidence: lib/articles/trial/store.ts:707 The order open, framed, sealed, exec, closed is declared once (line 14), and the expensive exec is gated on the seal.
